meta.title: Bandwidth ECG — Your network, on ECG. · for macOS
meta.description: A real-time ECG for your home network. Track bandwidth peaks, spot latency arrhythmias, and answer the question: do I really need to upgrade?

hero.titleZh: A diagnostic monitor for your bandwidth.
hero.subtitle: Track bandwidth peaks, detect lag arrhythmias, and answer — with data — the one question: do I actually need to upgrade my plan?

features.sectionSubtitle: Six continuous measurements, from live rhythm to long-term trend. Each one reads like a report you can actually use.

items.title: Real-time rhythm
items.subtitle: Menu-bar readout
items.description: Up/down speeds sampled at 1 Hz and shown live in the menu bar. No window required.

items.title: Peak capture
items.subtitle: Daily & all-time
items.description: Automatically logs daily and all-time peak throughput so you can tell if your plan still has headroom.

items.title: Rhythm strips
items.subtitle: 1m → 24h windows
items.description: Six time windows — 1m / 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 min / 24h — to see both micro-spikes and long-term shape.

items.title: Approach alert
items.subtitle: Amber / Red
items.description: As usage approaches your plan ceiling, readings turn Amber, then Red — just like a patient monitor.

items.title: Local chart
items.subtitle: No cloud, ever
items.description: Every reading stays in ~/Library. No accounts, no telemetry, no uploads. Period.

items.title: Low-draw instrument
items.subtitle: CPU <1%, RAM <50MB
items.description: Built on native APIs. You'll forget it's running — which is the point of a good monitor.

howItWorks.sectionSubtitle: Check in, attach the electrodes, read the report. Three steps, about 90 seconds.

steps.label: INTAKE
steps.title: Attach the electrodes
steps.description: Grab the DMG from GitHub and drop it in Applications. The app takes over the menu bar — no Dock clutter.

steps.label: CALIBRATION
steps.title: Enter your plan's ceiling
steps.description: Tell it your plan's rated speed (say, 500 Mbps) so the instrument knows when to raise an alert.

steps.label: DIAGNOSIS
steps.title: Live diagnostic readout
steps.description: From then on, every glance is a check-up. Upgrade decisions become data-driven — not vibes.

chartDemo.sectionSubtitle: A realistic bandwidth trace — calm baseline, sharp peaks, the occasional spike. Exactly what you want to read at a glance.

faq.sectionTitleZh: The five questions we get most
faq.sectionSubtitle: The five questions we get most.

items.question: Is this really free?
items.answer: Yes — 100% free and open source. No subscription, no in-app purchase, no ads.

items.question: Does my data leave my computer?
items.answer: No. Readings are stored only in ~/Library/Application Support/BandwidthECG on your Mac. This is not a cloud service.

items.question: Which macOS versions work?
items.answer: macOS 13.0 (Ventura) and later. Apple Silicon and Intel are both native.

items.question: Will it slow down my Mac?
items.answer: It won't. Monitoring uses native APIs — typically under 1% CPU and under 50 MB of RAM.

items.question: How do I fully uninstall?
items.answer: Drop the app in the Trash. To clear all recorded readings too, remove ~/Library/Application Support/BandwidthECG.

download.sectionSubtitle: Free. Local. Open source. Starting today, decide with data — not gut feel.

footer.disclaimer: Not a medical device. For network health only.
